about.title: About MathGraph — and how to contribute
about.heading: About MathGraph
about.p1: Mathematics is built step by step: axioms and definitions lead to theorems, theorems to further theorems, and every theorem rests on a proof. Yet theorems are usually taught as isolated facts.
about.p2: MathGraph shows the structure instead. Every box is an axiom, definition, theorem, proof or conjecture, and every line shows what depends on what. Click a box to see its statement, its source and how it connects to the rest.
about.exploreText: You don't need an account to read the graph, the open submissions, their discussions or the full change history.
about.step1: Create an account with your real name and a university email, then confirm the email.
about.step2: Open Submissions in the top-right corner of the graph and choose Make submission.
about.step3: Pick the type, write the statement (use $...$ for formulas), add a source, and link it to the boxes it uses, proves or belongs to.
about.step4: Other reviewers approve, reject, comment and suggest edits. You can accept a suggested edit at any time.
about.step5: After three approvals the submission joins the graph.
about.accountabilityText: Everyone's real name is shown next to their submissions, votes and comments, and every change is recorded in the public change history.
